root_cause: Assuming ASN1_STRING_get0_data() returns a NUL-terminated string and using strcmp() on it without first validating the string's explicit length field, when ASN1_STRING objects only guarantee explicit length tracking, not NUL termination.
findings: The code added to ossl_x509_check_cert_time() (and mirrored in ossl_x509_check_certificate_times) treats the raw data buffer returned by ASN1_STRING_get0_data() on the certificate's notAfter field as a NUL-terminated C string and passes it to strcmp() to compare against the literal "99991231235959Z". ASN1_STRING objects are NOT guaranteed to be NUL-terminated and their length is tracked explicitly
